gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Autour One has a bold, single-weight outline feel, with no hairlines. Noto Sans Oriya, with generous curve gaps and lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals, is where the pair's openness lives.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Noto Sans Osmanya has wide, easy s turns and a lowercase that looks oversized next to its capitals. And across a full page, the text keeps moving easily beneath Autour One's marker-traced strokes.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hm: Chunky and uniform, Autour One has no swell on any downstroke. Shrink the heading and that bold weight loses its punch, while Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong, a sans with a high x-height, stays the easier read.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-phoenicia: Autour One is all constant stroke weight, no sparkle, bold and round. Noto Sans Phoenician follows with generous lowercase height and s curves that open wide at both ends, which is the pair's real strength.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-sc: Noto Sans SC has chalk-like curves that stop well short of closing. Autour One's hairline-free, swell-free letters carry the weight, so the text below can stay modest in size and quiet.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Fat, round, drawn with one tip, Autour One announces itself. Noto Sans Sinhala, a sans-serif with a thick, dark band of lowercase and curve endings that stay well apart, can sit a size or two smaller.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Text here goes down easily on screens, with a sizable x-height, curves left unclosed. Noto Sans Soyombo carries that quietly while Autour One, with no heavy-to-light shift in any stroke, supplies the bold voice.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar is a sans-serif with curves that leave daylight. Beneath Autour One's uniform strokes, those short ascender stems on lowercase bodies let text move along smoothly, line after line.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-syriac-we: Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far from the stroke body. Noto Sans Syriac Western handles the compact, tall-bodied text while Autour One, each stroke held to one thickness, handles bold display.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Autour One draws tubelike, constant-weight lines that look bold and round. Noto Sans Tagalog, a sans whose middle zone dominates each line and whose curves stay generous, reads comfortably over paragraph after paragraph.
